# Roadmap

# Simplified Box Notation (SBN)

## `CORRECTION` + `CONJUNCTION`

```{.sbn code-line-numbers="false"}
boy.n.01                       % The boy
time.n.08 TPR now              %
    CORRECTION <1              %
sneeze.v.01 Agent -2 Time -1   % sneezed,
    CONJUNCTION <2             % I mean,
cough.v.01 Agent -3 Time -2    % coughed
```

## Research Questions {style="text-align: center;"}

::: {.r-fit-text}
1. **Representation**: How should within-clause RSR be represented in SBN, and what are the coverage and limitations of the representation?
2. **Parsing**: How well can LLM-based semantic parsers learn this representation from synthesised meaning-banked data, and what errors remain?
:::

## Abstract Description 

:::{.text-center}

$$
K = K_{\pi_{\text{pre}}} \land \neg K_{\pi_m} \land \big(K_{\pi_n} \land K_{\pi_{\text{post}}}\big) \land \varphi_{\mathit{Corr}(\pi_m,\pi_n)}
$$
:::

where: 
$K_{\pi_m}$ represents the reparandum
$K_{\pi_{\text{post}}}$ represents the repair

I put the abstract definition after the example to let the audience develop the gist first. Even if they fail to catch the logic expression, it doesn't obsticle the later parts. -- Does it work?
